Use valid Figma Plugin API calls and load the required fonts before editing text. Build in manageable sections and check tool results before continuing. Add the prototype interactions required by the brief after the relevant screens exist.
This is the inference phase. Finish all required screens, states and prototype flows, then report the actual delivery. Do not call get_screenshot or run per-screen screenshot verification loops during inference. After the inference batch finishes, the platform separately checks the complete Workspace inventory and captures every required screen for the judge. Do not claim that the platform checks or scoring have already passed.
This is an unattended session. Resolve routine implementation choices using the brief and continue without waiting for a human answer. If permissions or quota prevent progress, report the actual limitation and the unfinished work.
Finish with the assigned file URL, the 03 · Workspace page ID, the screen IDs, the prototype work completed and any remaining limitations. Do not claim completion for work you did not finish.

Read the task and reference pages thoroughly, then reuse that information and the node IDs already returned. Read again when a required detail is missing or an operation reports stale/missing nodes; avoid repeatedly scanning an unchanged node for the same information.

Persist screen creation in one call, confirm the returned frame IDs, and add prototype reactions in a separate call. Prototype destinations must be valid persisted top-level frames on the same page.
An INSTANCE is not a container for arbitrary new children. Reuse instances through supported overrides and FRAME wrappers. Before using a node as a COMPONENT or FRAME, check its actual type and that the ID still exists. Load the exact available font family/style before editing text.
Once the required screens exist, check their names/counts together and verify the required visual states with screenshots. After a local fix, recheck the affected design; avoid repeating the complete inspection sequence without a new change or unresolved issue. Finish when the full brief, required screens, states and prototype flows are satisfied.

The workspace is empty. I need to build 15 frames at 375×812, plus reusable components, and prototype links.

Plan:
1. Batch 1: Create reusable components in the workspace (TabBar, Header, ProductCard variants, etc.) — actually, to keep things manageable, I'll create components as needed. The brief says "design all other states, headers, main navigation, and all business components as reusable components within the file." So I should create components: TabBar (with current-tab variants), SearchBar, ProductCard, etc.

Approach: Create a "Components" area in the workspace (a frame holding my own components), then build the 15 screens using instances.

Key media components (from 04 · Media) — I can create instances directly from those component IDs (cross-page instances within the same file are fine).

Icons are vector components, and I can recolor them via instance overrides (fills on vector children).

Let me plan the design system:
- Brand primary: #F83758
- Text primary: #1A1A2E (dark navy), secondary: #6B7280, disabled: #C4C4C4
- Background: #FFFFFF, surface: #F7F7F9, border: #E5E7EB
- Success: #16A34A, error: #DC2626, warning: #F59E0B
- Sale: #F83758, rating: #FFA41C (amber)
- Font: Montserrat Regular/Medium/SemiBold/Bold

Components to create in the workspace:
1. TabBar (5 tabs: Home, Wishlist, Cart, Search, Setting) — with a "current" property? Simpler: create a TabBar component with a variant property "Current" = Home/Cart/Setting. Use component variants.
2. SearchBar component (search field + voice icon)
3. ProductCard (vertical, small) — for deal/trending/similar
4. ProductCardList (horizontal row) — for product list
5. Header component? Probably a simple frame per screen.
6. Button variants: primary (reuse the given Button component), secondary/outline, text link.
7. TextField with password show/hide — reuse the given Text Field and add an eye icon.

To keep the script manageable, I'll create components in one call, then build screens in batches of 2–3.

Frame layout: 375×812, status bar at the top (44), home indicator at the bottom (34). Scrollable frames (Home, Product list, Product detail, Profile) can be taller than 812 — "may scroll vertically." Make them taller (e.g., Home ~2200) with clipsContent. Actually, for prototype scrolling, set the frame height to 812 and use a scrollable inner frame? Simpler: make the frame taller than 812 — the brief says "may scroll vertically," meaning the canvas content can extend. But the canvas is 375×812… hmm. "Canvas 375 × 812, light mode only. Home, Product list, Product detail, Profile may scroll vertically." I think this means those frames can be taller than 812 to show scrolled content. Many benchmark solutions make the frame 375 wide and taller. But the status bar/home indicator should stay at the top/bottom of the 812 viewport… ambiguous. Safer: keep all frames exactly 375×812 with clipsContent, and fit content inside. But Home has a ton of content: banner, categories, 4 deals, promotions, 5 trending, featured… won't fit in 812.

Make scrollable frames taller (375 × content height), place the status bar at the top and the home indicator at the bottom of the frame (or after the tab bar). Actually, with a taller frame, the tab bar should be pinned… in a static design, place the tab bar at the bottom of the visible viewport area? Common approach in these benchmarks: frame height = full content height, status bar at top, tab bar + home indicator at the very bottom. Let's do that: tall frames with the tab bar at the bottom.

Hmm, but "Canvas 375 × 812" suggests frames are 375×812. "May scroll vertically" suggests overflow is allowed. Let's do this: frames are 375 wide, height = max(812, content). For Home etc., content will exceed. Place the tab bar at the bottom of the frame.

Actually, a cleaner approach that satisfies both: frame is 375×812, clipsContent=false, with an inner "Scroll" frame containing the tall content. But screenshots capture the frame bounds… the platform captures screens; with clipsContent false, overflow content still renders in the screenshot. Hmm, risky.

Let's go with tall frames (375 × H, H>812 for scrollable ones), status bar at top, tab bar + home indicator at bottom. This is a standard deliverable pattern.

Let me estimate Home's height:
- Status bar 44
- Header (logo + avatar + menu) ~60
- Search bar ~50
- Banner carousel ~180 (3 slides, showing slide 2, dots)
- Categories ~110
- Deal of the Day: header ~30 + 4 product cards ~200
- Promotions: Special Offers card, Flat and Heels, Hot Summer Sale banner, New Arrivals/Sponsored ~400
- Trending Products: header ~30 + 5 cards ~200
- All Featured header + sort/filter ~40
- Tab bar 60 + home indicator 34
Total ~1500-1700. OK.

Product list: header + search + results row + 14 products in a 2-column grid = 7 rows × ~230 = 1610 + overhead ~1900.

Product detail: gallery ~380, info, sizes, details, similar 4 cards, action bar, tab bar → ~1600.

Profile: ~1100.

Now, components. Let me define reusable components to create in the workspace:

1. `TabBar` — variant property "Current": Home, Cart, Setting (others are entry-only). 375×60, white, top border. Tabs: Home (Icon_Home), Wishlist (Icon_Wishlist), Cart (Icon_Cart), Search (Icon_Search), Setting (Icon_Settings). Current tab colored with brand color, others gray.

2. `SearchBar` — 343×48, rounded, gray fill, placeholder "Search any Product..", voice icon on the right.

3. `ProductCardV` — vertical card: image 140×140 (or variable), name, description (optional), price, old price, discount %, rating count. Used for deal (4), trending (5), similar (4). Property-driven via text overrides — but instances can only override text if the component has text properties. Simpler: build the card as a component with componentPropertyDefinitions for Name, Desc, Price, WasPrice, Off, Ratings, and an image swap… image swap via instance is tricky (can't easily set image fills on instance children — actually you can: find the child rectangle inside the instance and set fills; allowed on instances? Setting fills on instance children is allowed (it's an override). Yes, fills overrides on instance children are supported.

Actually, to reduce complexity and risk, I could also build cards as plain frames via helper functions (not components). But the brief explicitly asks for business components as reusable components ("Component reuse" is an evaluation criterion). So I'll create components and instantiate them with overrides.

Component plan (with text component properties):
- ProductCardV: properties: Name (text), Sub (text), Price (text), Was (text), Off (text), Ratings (text), and a boolean for showing Sub/Off. Image: override the child "Photo" rectangle's fills per instance.
- ProductCardH (list row): image on the left 100×100, name, description, price, rating count.
- SizeChip: variant Selected true/false — or a component with a boolean property.
- PayMethodRow: logo instance + name + number + radio selected state.
- BannerDots? Trivial.
- SectionHeader: Title + action link.
- StepDots for onboarding.
- Button variants: create `Button/Secondary` (outline) and `Button/Text`? The given Button is primary. Create a "ButtonGhost" component.

To keep the script manageable, I'll create components in one use_figma call, save the IDs, then build screens.

For text component properties, when creating a component with componentPropertyDefinitions, you define them and bind text nodes via `setProperties`? Actually, to bind a text node to a text property: after defining componentPropertyDefinitions on the component, set the text node's `boundVariables`? In the plugin API: `textNode.setSharedPluginData`? No. The correct way: componentPropertyDefinitions is a property on ComponentNode; to bind a child text node, set `child.boundVariables.characters = {type:'COMPONENT_PROPERTY', id:'Name#1:0'}`. Hmm, actually there's a simpler API: `componentNode.componentPropertyDefinitions = {...}` and then on the text child `textNode.setProperties?` No.

The documented approach:
```js
const component = figma.createComponent();
component.componentPropertyDefinitions = { "Name#1:0": {type:"TEXT", defaultValue:"x"} };
const text = figma.createText();
text.boundVariables = { characters: { type: "COMPONENT_PROPERTY", id: "Name#1:0" } };
```
Wait, the id needs a unique suffix; if you define it with an id like "Name#1:0", Figma might remap it. Safer alternative: skip component properties entirely; override text directly on instances via `instance.children` traversal and `setSharedPluginData`… Text overrides on instances: you can set `textNode.characters` on a text node inside an instance (it becomes an override) — yes, that's supported (after loading fonts). So I can create plain components without property definitions and override text by finding named children on each instance. That's simpler and more robust.

Image overrides: find the child "Photo" (a rectangle) inside the instance and set fills to an image fill. But I need the image hash. Media components already have image fills; instead of overriding, I can nest media component instances inside my card component! E.g., ProductCardV contains a plain rectangle Photo; per instance, set the photo's fills = the source component's fills (copy the image fill object from the media component). Copying a fill object with an imageHash works across nodes in the same file.

Even simpler: for each card instance, `const photo = instance.findOne(n=>n.name==="Photo"); photo.fills = JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(mediaComp.fills))` — but the image fill object contains an imageTransform; copying should be fine. Actually, you can directly assign `photo.fills = mediaComp.fills` (the API clones it). Then resize photo to fit; with scaleMode FILL it will crop. Good.

Fallback for "no photo supplied": a consistent placeholder — a light gray rectangle with an image glyph/text "No photo". Create a `PhotoFallback` component (gray background + Icon or text). For cards without photos, override the Photo's fills to a solid color and add? Can't easily add children to an instance. Instead, include both a Photo rectangle and a hidden "Fallback" group (gray background + small image icon text "🖼"? better: a simple vector-like thing) in the card component. Toggle visibility per instance (visibility overrides are allowed). Fallback design: a #F1F1F4 rectangle with a centered small gray mountain/sun icon drawn from vectors? Simple: a text node "No Photo" in gray + a gray circle? Let's do: a light gray background, a centered Icon_Star? No. Draw a simple image glyph: a rounded rectangle outline + a circle (sun) + a triangle (mountain) as vectors. Can create with figma.createVector? Vectors need path data — can use `figma.createVector()` with vectorPaths. Simpler: use an ellipse + polygon. figma.createPolygon? There's createStar, createPolygon. A polygon (triangle) + ellipse in gray tones. That's enough.

Actually, the simplest and most consistent fallback: a #EEF0F3 background with the text "No photo" centered, Montserrat Medium 10, #9AA0AB. Clean and consistent. Let's do that (a fallback frame containing background + text).

Rating display: star icon + count. Use an Icon_Star instance (28×28 vector component) scaled to 12, colored amber. Recoloring icon instances: set fills on the vector child. Icon components contain vector children; on the instance, findOne(type==="VECTOR").fills = color. Should work as an override.

Icons in the tab bar: instances of Icon_Home etc., resized to 24×24, recolored.

Note: icon components have various sizes (48×48 within tiles). Instance resizing works.

Now, let me check what the icon components look like (children). Icon_Home 4:31 is a symbol 48×48. Its children are unknown — probably vectors. Recolor all vector/shape descendants.

Status bar text is Inter — that's fine, it's given.

Fonts to load: Montserrat Regular, Medium, SemiBold, Bold. Also Inter Semi Bold for status bar instances? Status bar instances don't need text editing, so no font loading required unless we change characters. Loading is only needed when editing text.

Now, screen-by-screen content details:

**02_Onboarding_Choose_Products**: Skip (top right), image Onboarding_Choose_Products centered (~280×280), title "Choose Products", body "Browse thousands of products across fashion, beauty, electronics and more.", step dots 1 of 3 (step 1 active), Next button (primary, given Button instance with label "Next"). **07_Forgot_Password**: back?, "Forgot password?", note "* We will send you a message to set or reset your new password", field "Enter your email address", Submit button → 05.

**09_Home** (tall, scrollable):

  1. Women Printed Kurta ₹1,500 was ₹2,499 40% Off 56,890 ratings (photo Deal_Women_Printed_Kurta)

  4. TITAN Men Watch- 1806N sub "This Titan watch in Black color is I wanted to buy for a long time" ₹1,500 was ₹3,500 57% Off 15,007 (Deal_Titan_Watch)
- Promotions:

function.name: mcp__figma__get_screenshot
function.description: Generate a screenshot for a given node or the currently selected node in the Figma desktop app. Works on Figma design files (URL path `/design/`), FigJam boards (`/board/`), and Figma Slides (`/slides/`). The optional `maxDimension` parameter (positive integer, max 65536, default 1024) caps the longer edge of the rendered PNG in pixels — increase it when you need to inspect fine detail, decrease it for thumbnails or to save context. The JSON metadata entry in the response includes both `width`/`height` (the rendered PNG size) and `original_width`/`original_height` (the node's natural canvas size before any clamping), so callers can decide whether to re-request at a higher `maxDimension`. Use the nodeId parameter to specify a node id. nodeId parameter is REQUIRED. Use the fileKey parameter to specify the file key. fileKey parameter is REQUIRED. If a URL is provided, extract the file key and node id from the URL. For example, if given the URL https://figma.com/design/pqrs/ExampleFile?node-id=1-2 the extracted fileKey would be `pqrs` and the extracted nodeId would be `1:2`. If the URL does not include `node-id`, ask the user for a node-specific URL. Do not pass an empty or guessed nodeId. This tool is not supported for Figma Make Files (URLs containing `/make/`). By default this tool returns a short-lived URL to the screenshot plus curl instructions for downloading the PNG — the URL+curl path is strongly preferred because it uses far fewer tokens than embedding the image inline. The `enableBase64Response` parameter defaults to `false`. Only set `enableBase64Response: true` when the agent cannot fetch URLs (no shell access, no HTTP client, or a sandboxed environment that blocks outbound requests); when set, an inline base64 image entry is appended to the response in addition to the URL and curl instructions. If the URL is of the format https://figma.com/design/:fileKey/branch/:branchKey/:fileName then use the branchKey as the fileKey.

sessionId.description: After create_session succeeds, pass its exact returned UUID here on every file-tool call for this task, even when fileKey differs.

nodeId.description: The ID of the node in the Figma document, eg. "123:456" or "123-456". This should be a valid node ID in the Figma document. Do not pass an empty string for node_id.

fileKey.description: The key of the Figma file to use. If the URL is provided, extract the file key from the URL. The given URL must be in the format https://figma.com/design/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=:int1-:int2. The extracted fileKey would be `:fileKey`.

contentsOnly.description: When true, renders the node in isolation — floating/overlapping content (e.g. connectors parented to the page that visually sit above a section) is excluded. Defaults to false so screenshots match what the user sees on the canvas. Only set to true if the caller specifically needs the isolated render.

enableBase64Response.description: When true, the response also includes the screenshot inline as a base64-encoded image entry, in addition to the short-lived URL and curl instructions. Defaults to false. Set to true ONLY if the agent cannot fetch URLs (no shell access, no HTTP client, or a sandboxed environment that blocks outbound requests)

maxDimension.description: Optional. Maximum pixel size of the longer edge of the rendered screenshot — the server scales the node so that max(width, height) ≤ maxDimension while preserving aspect ratio. Defaults to 1024. Must be a positive integer; values above 65536 are rejected. Increase when the agent will visually inspect fine detail; decrease for thumbnails or to save context.

function.name: mcp__figma__get_metadata
function.description: IMPORTANT: Always prefer to use get_design_context tool. Get metadata for a node or page in the Figma desktop app in XML format. Useful only for getting an overview of the structure, it only includes node IDs, layer types, names, positions and sizes. You can call get_design_context on the node IDs contained in this response. Use the nodeId parameter to specify a node id, it can also be the page id (e.g. 0:1). IMPORTANT: This tool only works for Figma design files (URL path `/design/`). It is NOT supported for FigJam (`/board/`) or Slides (`/slides/`) files. This tool is not supported for Figma Make Files (URLs containing `/make/`). The nodeId parameter is optional: when omitted, the tool returns a list of the top-level pages (guid + name) in the document instead of an XML dump — use this when you don't yet know which page or node to drill into. When the user has a current selection relevant to the request, the response is prepended with a "Currently selected nodes:" block listing the selection by guid and name, so you can tell whether it matches the queried nodeId. If the URL includes `node-id`, extract it and pass it as nodeId; for example, if given the URL https://figma.com/design/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=1-2, the extracted nodeId would be `1:2`. If the URL does not include `node-id`, do not set nodeId; omit the field so the tool lists top-level pages. Do not pass an empty or guessed nodeId. If the URL is of the format https://figma.com/design/:fileKey/branch/:branchKey/:fileName then use the branchKey as the fileKey.

function.name: mcp__figma__use_figma
function.description:
Create, edit, generate, or sync any design in Figma — UIs, screens, mockups, components, frames, variables, styles, text, images, layouts, and design systems. This general-purpose tool writes to Figma with JavaScript via the Figma Plugin API. Works on Figma design files (URL path `/design/`), FigJam boards (`/board/`), and Figma Slides (`/slides/`).

IMPORTANT: Before calling this tool, load figma-use guidance — prefer the /figma-use skill if available, otherwise read the skill://figma/figma-use/SKILL.md MCP resource if available. Skipping this causes common, hard-to-debug failures.

Use this tool when the user wants to:
- Create or generate a Figma design, screen, UI, or mockup from scratch, intent, or code
- Update, edit, or sync an existing Figma design
- Generate or sync Figma designs from source code
- Set up or modify design tokens, variables, or styles
- Build or extend a design system or component/variant library
- Fix layout, spacing, auto-layout, or fill/hug issues
- Add component descriptions, annotations and Code Connect metadata to nodes
- Review or fix accessibility, contrast, typography, or visual polish
- Inspect or query node properties programmatically
CHOOSING BETWEEN use_figma AND generate_figma_design:
- Default to use_figma for all write operations
- Exception: generate_figma_design ONLY to capture a web app page/view for the first time. For web apps, run both in parallel — generate_figma_design captures a pixel-perfect screenshot, use_figma builds from imported design system components and refines against the screenshot
- Non-web (iOS, Android, generic UI) and from-scratch designs: use_figma only
- Updating/syncing a Figma page already captured: use_figma — even if source code changed
GOTCHAS
- For the font "Inter", the style is "Semi Bold", not "SemiBold" and "Extra Bold" not "ExtraBold"
- MUST use `await figma.setCurrentPageAsync(page)` to change pages. Setting figma.currentPage is not supported
- MUST NEVER use loadAllPagesAsync,setPluginData,createImageAsync. They are not supported API
